speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Donald Trump wants to end birthright citizenship.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Left-wing media and Democrats are fighting it tooth and nail

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: because illegals, indeed criminals, are their mother's milk.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Among Donald Trump's first avalanche of executive orders

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: was one ending birthright citizenship,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: the policy where almost anybody born on U.S. soil

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: automatically gets citizenship.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: The practice itself comes from a misreading of the 14th Amendment,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: which granted citizenship to freed slaves,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: specifically to, quote,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: all persons born in the United States

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: and subject to the jurisdiction thereof.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: The key phrase here is subject to the jurisdiction.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: That's long been understood to exclude diplomats,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: so birth alone is not enough,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: but jurisdiction is actually a whole lot more limiting.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Historian Tom Wood cites the authors of the 14th Amendment,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: who said, quote,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: this will not, of course, include persons born in the United States

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: who are foreigners or aliens,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: because it only applies to people, quote,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: not owing allegiance to any foreign sovereignty.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: In other words, if you have citizenship of another country, say Mexico,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: you are not under the jurisdiction, according to the 14th.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Why?

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Because the point of the 14th was to give citizenship to former slaves

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: who held no other citizenship.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Now, notably, for 50 years after the 14th,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Indians were not given birthright citizenship,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: specifically because they were citizens of another nation,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: the Navajo, Comanche, Seminole.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: And when they were given birthright citizenship,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: it was by act of Congress, not the 14th.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Of course, not only are legal subject to the jurisdiction of another country,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: they are in this country illegally.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: They are literally fugitives from the law,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: the very definition of not under the jurisdiction.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Now, this all matters because so-called birthright citizenship

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: is one of the most abused parts of our immigration system.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Every year, roughly 622,000 people are born to non-citizen parents,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: of which 400,000 to illegals.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: That comes to one in six births in the country.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: In the case of illegals, anchor babies become a jackpot.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: One study found 75% of migrants from Guatemala and Mexico with children

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: are on federal welfare programs,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: adding up to hundreds of billions in costs.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Indeed, we've heard stories from Biden's illegals

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: where young women in shelters try to get knocked up

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: by pretty much anybody to get that precious anchor baby,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: your tax dollars at work.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: The abuse extends to an estimated 40,000 so-called birth tourists

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: who literally fly to America on vacation,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: give birth, and go home with the status of parents of an American citizen

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: despite having spent mere days in the country.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: This is a full-on industry in China and Taiwan

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: where pre-birthing centers are common,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: kind of an assisted care for pregnant women.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: But instead of doing it in China,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: they fly to a center in LA,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: fully staffed by Chinese,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: and presto, they get all the benefits of citizenship.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: All in between the illegals, temporary visas like H-1Bs or students

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: and birth tourists,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: one in six new Americans either should not be here

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: or have almost no connection to the country.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: So it's next, brought to you by Unchain.com.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: The left will go to war on this because they know

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: the vast majority of beneficiaries will vote left.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: The case they'll keep citing is Wong Kim Ark from 1873,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: which grants citizenship to the child of permanent residence,

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: something most Americans are probably fine with

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: and something that has nothing to do

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: with these 622,000 illegals and tourists abusing the system.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Okay, we'll be watching.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: See you next time.
